title: Fireflies Light Up Tomorrowland: Martin Garrix and U2’s The Edge Surprise Fans!
summary: Have you ever seen fireflies blink on a summer night? Now imagine that magical feeling turned into a song — and played by one of the world’s biggest DJs with a rock star! That’s exactly what happened at Tomorrowland, a huge music festival in Belgium. On Friday, Martin Garrix, a 30-year-old DJ known for his energetic beats, surprised everyone by bringing out The Edge, the guitarist from the legendary band U2. Together, they performed a brand-new track called “Fireflies.” The crowd went wild as The Edge’s famous guitar sound mixed with Garrix’s electronic music. The song also features the voice of Bono, U2’s lead singer, but his part was recorded ahead of time. Garrix later posted on social media that the song will be “out soon,” and fans can already pre-save it. This isn’t the first time Garrix and U2 have teamed up. They made a soccer anthem called “We Are the People” for the UEFA 2020 tournament, and Garrix produced U2’s song “Your Song Saved My Life” for the movie Sing 2. Bono has also helped write some of Garrix’s other songs. So, what’s next? Nobody knows for sure if “Fireflies” is just a single, part of Garrix’s new album, or even a sneak peek from U2’s upcoming album. U2 just released a happy new song called “Street of Dreams” and are working on a “noisy, messy, unreasonably colorful” album to celebrate their 50th anniversary. Bono says they want to make vivid rock & roll as “an act of resistance against all this awfulness on our small screens.” Sounds like they’re ready to shake things up — and maybe light up the night like fireflies!
why_it_matters: When musicians from different styles team up, they create fresh sounds that can inspire you to mix your own ideas in school projects or hobbies.
